newsitem.title: GERMANY: Turkey's Kurdish rebel chief wants Kurds to unite.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Kurdish rebel chief wants Kurds to unite.

text.p: Turkey's Kurdish rebel leader said in an interview broadcast on Friday that his Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) would put pressure on Iraq's rival groups to end their conflict and join forces to work for Kurdish independence.
"We will use our political and military weight on both sides to try to end the conflict," Abdullah Ocalan told German ZDF television in remarks translated into German.

Ocalan's PKK has been fighting Ankara for 12 years for Kurdish autonomy in southeastern Turkey, a region which borders the restive Kurdish region of northern Iraq and also areas populated by Kurds in Iran and Syria.

Iraq's President Saddam Hussein last week sent troops to northern Iraq to help the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) inflict a heavy defeat on the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), incurring a military response from the United States.
Ocalan said he had often urged Iraq's rival groups to join in a joint Kurdish security and cooperation council.
He said the conflict in Iraq was harming the cause of Kurdish independence -- and that his own PKK must be involved in a joint effort to reach that goal.
"Democracy must be established. The Kurdish problem cannot be solved by one person alone," he said. "We need a broad consensus... No one side must be the victor over the other."
"At the moment, people are trying to solve the Kurdish problem without the PKK. But that will not happen," he said.
"I believe now is the time to take steps to solve the Kurdish problem."
Ocalan said he had offered advice to KDP leader Massoud Barzani, who has enlisted the help of his former adversary Saddam to push back the PUK.
"Even if you have sole power, the Iraqi government will still fight you, and that will put you in an even more difficult situation," Ocalan said he had told Barzani.
